Subject: Post-incident summary: conversation fragmentation root cause & next steps

Team / Atlas execs —

Follow-up and summary from the incident yesterday (timeline condensed):

Timeline (UTC):
- 2026-12-07T15:37Z: Canary deploy changed per-route limiter token bucket (intended to reduce burst traffic).
- 2026-12-07T15:52Z: Autoscaler scaled-down transient worker pool; some new workers came up cold.
- 2026-12-07T15:52–16:10Z: 429s spike observed on us-west-2 edges; client retries triggered backpressure and a retry amplification loop.
- 2026-12-07T15:58Z: Several streams were reset due to proxy FIN/RST causing client-side idle disconnects and partial tokens being duplicated when retries succeeded.

Root cause: A misconfigured limiter rule in the canary caused aggressive 429 responses to a subset of requests; combined with a recent transient scale-down (cold cache) this resulted in client retries amplifying load and fragmenting streams mid-response. In short: configuration + scale timing + imperfect client backoff created the retry storm and idle disconnects.

Immediate remediation performed:
- Rolled back the limiter change within 10m of detection.
- Enabled streaming->polling fallback for Atlas routes for a 30m window.
- Warmed KV caches on freshly started nodes and adjusted keepalive settings on the edge.
- Issued temporary client guidance: increase timeout to 45s and enable jittered backoff in SDK.

Follow-ups (owner):
- (Neha) Add config validation gates to prevent limiter rules that return 429s under normal steady-state traffic (ETA: 2 weeks).
- (Sean) Add automated warmup hooks for new worker nodes to pre-populate KV cache (ETA: 3 weeks).
- (Product) Ship SDK advisory for 429-aware backoff patterns and enable a feature flag for streaming fallback (ETA: 2 weeks).
- (Markus) Exec brief for Atlas and credit reconciliation (business operations) — I'll send a formal summary by EOD.

Attachments: incident_timeline_draft.pdf (contains trace snippets), atlas_session_logs_1207.zip (sample logs)

Closing notes: No customer data loss was found; transcripts were duplicated in places but we have tooling to dedupe post-hoc. We will follow up with a formal RCA and an action tracker.

—Markus Klein
VP, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
